title: State Management and Hooks
description: Learn how to manage component state using the useState and useEffect hooks to build interactive React Native applications.

lessons.title: What is State in React Native?
lessons.content: State represents the dynamic data in a component. It determines how the UI looks at a given time. When the state changes, the component re-renders to reflect the new data.

lessons.title: Introduction to useState Hook
Handling Multiple State Variables
Updating State Based on Previous State
lessons.content:
Use a callback function to update state based on the previous value.

```jsx
setCount(prevCount => prevCount + 1);
```

lessons.title: Introduction to useEffect Hook
lessons.content: The `useEffect` hook lets you run side effects like fetching data, subscriptions, or manually changing the DOM after every render or on specific state changes.

lessons.title: Using useEffect with Dependencies
useEffect for Component Mount and Unmount
Common State Patterns
lessons.content:
- Initialize state with proper defaults.
- Avoid storing derived data.
- Use objects or arrays for grouping related state values.

lessons.title: Controlled Components
lessons.content:
Use state to control form inputs.

```jsx
<TextInput value={text} onChangeText={setText} />
```

lessons.title: Best Practices for State and useEffect
lessons.content:
- Keep components focused and manageable.
- Extract logic into custom hooks if reused.
- Always clean up subscriptions or timers in `useEffect`.
